_meta.description: Fictional customer profiles used to make the business case concrete in the pitch. Not real companies — chosen to map directly to the three regulatory frameworks with the strongest narrative: RBI (BFSI), DPDP-general (MSME, an explicitly underserved segment), and CERT-In (Government, its broadest-reaching framework).

profiles.name: Suvidha Cooperative Bank
profiles.tagline: A mid-sized cooperative bank where 'the vendor IT doesn't know about yet' is a real RBI supervisory-action risk, not a hypothetical.
profiles.story: Suvidha Bank is RBI-regulated and must keep full end-to-end payment transaction data within India. Its Finance and Operations teams have quietly connected invoice-processing and legacy document tools over the years — exactly the kind of unmanaged vendor exposure RBI holds the bank fully accountable for, whether IT approved it or not.

profiles.name: Meridian Exports Pvt Ltd
profiles.tagline: A growing exporter with no dedicated security team — exactly the underserved segment every competitor prices out.
profiles.story: Meridian's Sales and Marketing teams juggle international clients across time zones, connecting CRM sync tools, translation services, and scheduling apps to move fast. None of it was ever centrally reviewed — a single dormant CRM export tool from a departed employee still holds customer PII today.

profiles.name: State Directorate of Digital Services
profiles.tagline: CERT-In's broadest-reaching framework applies here — and a 6-hour incident clock is unforgiving if the incident is hiding in an unmonitored tool.
profiles.story: The Directorate's engineering and HR teams have connected developer productivity tools and employee-engagement platforms independently. Under CERT-In, any of these becomes a reportable-incident risk the moment something goes wrong — and right now, nobody has a single list of what's actually connected.
